content.comment_body: Hello, I'm having trouble getting the analog filter to work in [product_name] [version_no]. I tried both types of analog inputs, but can't get either to function—values are stuck at zero. Any ideas?
Welcome to the forum. It's difficult to comment without seeing your setup or code. Could you clarify if the issue occurs during simulation or on your actual device?

Make sure you've configured your device to allow either 2 or 4 analog inputs. Inputs AI1 and AI2 correspond to specific terminals, while additional analog inputs also have designated terminals. Remember to configure and transfer these settings to your device.
Thanks for your reply. Here’s additional info: 1. Tests are being run with the real device. 2. I’ve attached a screenshot of the code.
Please provide a screenshot displaying the live values during Online Test.
Now, with live values shown: AM5 and AM6 always display identical readings.
What do you want to achieve using the analog filter feature? What is your main reason for using it?

I'm monitoring temperature readings that fluctuate quite a bit. The process runs slowly, so I'm hoping a filter can help stabilize the output. Applying a filter with a multi-second time constant would be ideal.
Consider using the "Average Value" block. It lets you average several readings over a set timeframe, which can help smooth your measurements.
That’s perfect—exactly what I needed! Just curious, is the filter function intended for high-frequency low-pass filtering?
It’s simply for averaging. The sampling interval and number of measurements determine the filter’s behavior; values are summed and divided to produce the smoothed result.
